standard.title: Specification for Iron Powder (Reduction Grade) (लोहे के बुरादे (अपचायक ग्रेड) की विशिष्टि) (First Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the physical form, chemical composition, quality tolerances, testing methods, and field sampling plans for iron powder (reduction grade) used primarily as a chemical reducing agent in chemical synthesis and industrial metallurgy.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the physical form, chemical composition, quality tolerances, testing methods, and field sampling plans for iron powder (reduction grade) used primarily as a chemical reducing agent in chemical synthesis and industrial metallurgy.

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this reaffirmed copy (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the prestigious 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) on HDPE bags or steel drums as a certified guarantee of material purity and high reduction activity. Additionally, compliance with IS 1612 is heavily integrated into commercial purchase contracts for dyestuffs, pharmaceutical intermediates, and chemical reagents across India.
requirements: Under this first revision, the maximum limit of carbon impurity is strictly lowered from 2.5 to 2.0 percent by mass to prevent filtration difficulties when isolating organic products.
A mandatory chemical reduction activity test is incorporated because iron powders with identical chemical purity and particle size can show significant differences in reduction efficiency.
The total elemental iron (Fe) content must satisfy a minimum specified percentage (nominally 93.0 percent by mass, with a tolerance of ±2.0 percent) to ensure adequate reducing equivalent.
Moisture and volatile components are restricted to a maximum of 0.50 percent by mass to maintain chemical stability and prevent rusting during storage.
Chemical assays must utilize concentrated hydrochloric acid conforming to IS 265, along with barium chloride, bromine solution, aluminium metal, and ammonium hydroxide.
Quantitatively determines phosphorus (percent by mass) using a volumetric back-titration of a digested sample with standard hydrochloric acid and a parallel control run.
To prevent ambient moisture absorption and premature oxidation, samples must not be drawn or prepared in an exposed place.
The sampling trier or instrument must be completely clean and dry before drawing material to avoid cross-contamination.
Volatile matter and elemental iron content tests must be carried out on each of the individual samples drawn from the consignment.
The remaining chemical characteristics, carbon impurities, and activity must be evaluated on the composite sample only.
All observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 to match the significant places of the specified limits.
